      <title>Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</link>
      <description><p>After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’</p><p>The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a>, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:14:38 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/6487803463c6c4e3138642f657eeb1cd90cd5acc/0_111_1078_862/master/1078.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=e825c93b0c4e49e69e380953e02995c6">

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:10:28 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Potential 'national security crisis' as Nvidia ex-CEO summoned by US Congress</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-potential-national-security-crisis-as-nvidia-ex-ceo-summoned-by-us-congress</link><description>
What began as an investigation into the now former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is turning into what could be shaping up to be a "national security crisis", says France 24's correspondent in Los Angeles Wassim Cornet, after US lawmakers called on Huang to face their questions in December. Huang resigned as head of the chip giant over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2bdc335e-df48-11f1-bf98-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261113-100555-100803-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2bdc335e-df48-11f1-bf98-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261113-100555-100803-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">30a21f98-df48-11f1-80f1-119d78160029</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:00:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>'One of the biggest outages ever': Disruption to Microsoft services enters second day</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-one-of-the-biggest-outages-ever-disruption-to-microsoft-services-enters-second-day</link><description>
An outage of Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot that began on Thursday continued to cause disruption to users around the world on Friday as the tech giant struggled to fix server problems it blamed for the problems. France 24’s tech correspondent Peter O’Brien takes a look at what we know about the outage which, given its scale and duration, makes it one of the “biggest ever”, he says.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cefb3d1c-df45-11f1-8907-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261113-100137-100517-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/cefb3d1c-df45-11f1-8907-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261113-100137-100517-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d3a35cb4-df45-11f1-b1ba-39b345448c8e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:59:22 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Winter is coming: Putin seeks to 'hammer Ukrainians, their power grid, their water supplies'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/winter-is-coming-putin-seeks-to-hammer-ukrainians-their-power-grid-their-water-supplies</link><description>
As renewed diplomatic efforts seek to bring an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, the prospect of a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing visions of European security and an increasingly unpredictable and pro-Moscow US. For Mark Galeotti, Executive Director of Mayak Intelligence and Honorary Professor at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies, Moscow's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. And the territorial dispute over Donbas presents a particularly formidable obstacle. Putin's determination to claim control over the entirety of the region confronts Ukraine's refusal to surrender territory it continues to hold.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/64f9ee20-df42-11f1-8bdb-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261112-151425-152330-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/64f9ee20-df42-11f1-8bdb-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261112-151425-152330-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6b46e210-df42-11f1-b32a-bddd65b33045</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:26:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴 Live: Microsoft 'not aware of any malicious activity' behind global Outlook outage</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/technology/20261113-major-microsoft-outlook-outage-disrupts-services-in-74-countries</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">e6493b2a-df42-11f1-bb72-1795f14a1068</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:18:23 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Who will inherit 007's licence to thrill? 'The world is not enough' in the hunt for James Bond</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/who-will-inherit-007-s-licence-to-thrill-the-world-is-not-enough-in-the-hunt-for-james-bond</link><description>
More than six decades after James Bond first appeared on the big screen, the search for Daniel Craig's successor has become a revealing debate about the future of one of cinema's most enduring, and endearing, franchises. "From the cold-blooded sexual magnetism of Sean Connery to the more tongue-in-cheek take of Roger Moore, to Daniel Craig's gritty realism, there's really a James Bond for everyone." But who will inherit the licence to thrill? FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes us on this exciting edge-of-your-seat adventure with a "view to a kill". Should Bond remain faithful to his traditional identity, or reinvent himself to reflect changing attitudes towards gender, diversity and contemporary heroism?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b9a9d7aa-df2e-11f1-9fbc-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261112-163722-164327-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b9a9d7aa-df2e-11f1-9fbc-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261112-163722-164327-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bf832302-df2e-11f1-93aa-ff49b899689e</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 07:04:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:03:59 +0000 en <![CDATA[ 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight ]]> SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic.

The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms.

On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X, and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic."

The phrase is familiar to fans of Douglas Adams' sci-fi classic "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy": In the novel, the electronic guidebook that helps travelers find their way across the cosmos has "Don't panic!" on its cover.

And Ship 42 itself is connected to the beloved book, by virtue of its serial number. In "The Hitchhiker's Guide," a supercomputer named Deep Mind is asked to come up with "the answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything." It thinks for 7.5 million years and comes up with "42."

SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has voiced his affection for "The Hitchhiker's Guide" in the past — and he has already paid tribute to it with a well-placed "Don't panic."

The debut launch of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket back in February 2018 sent Musk's red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the sun, with a spacesuit-clad mannequin named Starman at the wheel and its entertainment display programmed to read "Don't panic!"

Starship Flight 15 is scheduled to launch today during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). You can watch it here at Space.com.

If all goes according to plan, Starship's Super Heavy first stage will come back to Starbase for a chopsticks catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff.

Ship 42, meanwhile, will head to orbit, a destination that Starship reached for the first time on Flight 14, which took place on Sept. 28. Ship 42 will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites today — the second batch of the spacecraft to reach orbit. (The first set of 26 were delivered on Flight 14).

Ship 42 will stay up for a while after that, circling Earth 14 times before coming back for its own chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after launch.

That's the plan, anyway; SpaceX will only go through with a Ship catch attempt if all systems on the vehicle look good. If there are any problems, the company will divert to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, near either Hawaii or Chile.

Both of Starship's stages — Super Heavy and the Ship — are designed to be rapidly reusable. And "rapidly" is a bit of understatement: SpaceX wants to launch 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030, Musk has said.

The chopsticks-catch strategy is a big part of that vision. Bringing both Starship stages directly back to the launch mount will greatly reduce the time needed for inspection, refurbishment and reflight, according to SpaceX.

The company has already caught Super Heavy on three previous Starship test flights. It has never tried to do so with Ship, instead targeting ocean splashdowns with the upper stage.

The double catch attempt may be unprecedented, but SpaceX seems to be taking its own advice: There's no panic around Flight 15 or its bold goals.

"I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," Musk said last month, during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call.

SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.

Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before.

You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan.

Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight.

The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the company has said.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy, pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover.

So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description.

The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit.

The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28.

Ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff.

There's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile.

So it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Man of Tomorrow': Release date, plot, cast & everything we know about the 'Superman' sequel ]]> It feels like yesterday when we were discussing Superman, the first big-screen entry in James Gunn's rebooted DCU. Now Gunn is out, and Skydance (the company formed by the merger of Warner and Paramount) is already dismantling his grand plans for the DCU.

That means that Man of Tomorrow, which arrives next summer, will be the final entry in Gunn's ambitious, and occasionally divisive, DC experiment. The DCU's first chapter — officially titled 'Gods and Monsters' — gave us Supergirl and Clayface (as well as TV shows like Peacemaker S2 and Lanterns) in the run-up to Clark Kent and Lex Luthor's return.

Man of Tomorrow looks to be upping the stakes from Earthly villains to intergalactic baddies with the introduction of Brainiac, and it may well have been the herald of the first Justice League movie in the rebooted DCU.

Gunn has yet to prove audiences actually care about more than Batman and Supes, which might explain why this follow-up is also an ensemble of sorts. As the Marvel Cinematic Universe prepares to unleash Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars, and even a fresh X-Men reboot, their DC counterparts have always struggled to get their dream team off the ground.

We'll never know what might have been, but we can still enjoy Gunn's DC swansong when it lands in 2027. Here's everything we know about James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow.

When is Man of Tomorrow coming out?

Man of Tomorrow will be released theatrically in the United States on July 9, 2027. Most international territories are expected to get it around the same time.

Only a few months after Superman's release and successful box office run, DC Studios and Warner Bros. Pictures confirmed the sequel would be coming two years after Clark Kent's return to the big screen.

How to watch Man of Tomorrow

Man of Tomorrow isn't out yet, but you can watch the rest of the DCU so far (it's pretty good for the most part) in preparation first.

When the movie hits theaters on July 9, 2027, it'll likely remain exclusive to big screens for at least two or three months, depending on how successful it is.

With that said, we know Warner Bros. (now part of Skydance) isn't the most patient when it comes to theatrical runs based on its track record, so the chances are Man of Tomorrow will hit HBO Max sooner rather than later, probably by early autumn 2027.

Watch Superman and the rest of the DCU on HBO Max:

Basic (Ads): $10.99/month or $109.99/year
Standard (No Ads): $18.49/month or $184.99/year
Premium (4K): $22.99/month or $229.99/year

Is there a Man of Tomorrow trailer?

No, we're still waiting for the first Man of Tomorrow trailer. Looking at the timeline of Superman's fantastic marketing campaign, however, we can guess the sequel will get a first trailer before 2026 ends, probably in time for Christmas.

Is Brainiac the main villain in Man of Tomorrow?

Yes, James Gunn has officially confirmed Brainiac is the main threat Earth is facing in Man of Tomorrow. This explains why other heroes will be joining Superman in a fight against the alien mastermind, but the plot is looking a bit more complex.

In typical comic book fashion (and somewhat reminiscent of Thor: The Dark World), the main hook in Man of Tomorrow appears to be a reluctant alliance between the first movie's villain, Lex Luthor, and Kal-El (aka Clark Kent). "Enemies to allies" is always a fun dynamic to have in a sequel, especially when stars David Corenswet (Superman) and Nicholas Hoult (Lex Luthor) delivered strong and memorable performances the first time around.

The actual plot remains under wraps, but we can guess Brainiac — one of DC's biggest and most iconic alien villains — will be a tough nut to crack, thus requiring some sort of unofficial team-up that will include returning heroes like Mister Terrific, Guy Gardner, Hawkgirl, John Stewart, Blue Beetle, and even Kara Zor-El (Supergirl). There are other names circling the project that could lead to even bigger appearances, but don't expect to learn much about them before the movie's marketing kicks off.

Why should you care about Brainiac? Well, he's a super-intelligent techno-organic alien from the planet Colu with an obsession with knowledge and self-improvement. A perfect foe for Luthor, Earth's greatest mind, but also a breath of fresh air for Superman, who's been stuck battling either Kryptonian menaces or just Luthor too long on the big screen.

Who is in the cast of Man of Tomorrow?

As a direct continuation of Superman, Man of Tomorrow is bringing back plenty of actors in both main and supporting roles, including:

  • David Corenswet (Superman / Clark Kent / Kal-El)
  • Nicholas Hoult (Lex Luthor)
  • Rachel Brosnahan (Lois Lane)
  • Nathan Fillion (Guy Gardner / Green Lantern)
  • Edi Gathegi (Michael Holt / Mister Terrific)
  • Isabela Merced (Kendra Saunders / Hawkgirl)
  • Skyler Gisondo (Jimmy Olsen)
  • Frank Grillo (Rick Flag Sr.)
  • Sara Sampaio (Eve Teschmacher)
  • María Gabriela de la Faría (Angela Spica / The Engineer)
  • Neva Howell (Martha Kent)
  • Pruitt Taylor Vince (Pa Kent)
  • Wendell Pierce (Perry White)

New cast members with publicly announced (or previously established) characters include:

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 12, 2014: European Philae probe lands on Comet 67P, bounced twice and then got lost for nearly 2 years ]]>

On Nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P. To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement.

The European Space Agency's Philae lander separated from an orbiter called Rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired.

When it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space. The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down.

Philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it. Images from Rosetta showed Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet.

Why it mattered

The European Space Agency's Rosetta and Philae expedition was a first-of-its-kind mission, an endeavour to not just rendezvous with a comet and watch it change over time as it approached the sun (that was Rosetta's job), but also to soft-land a probe on its icy and rocky surface to see what a comet is truly made of.

The Rosetta and Philae mission succeeded on both counts, but Philae's historic landing was marred by its turbulent touchdown. Philae actually landed three different times on Comet 67/P, all because the harpoons designed to secure it in place didn't fire as planned.

After the first landing, Philae bounced up and drifted around the comet for two hours, making another bounce before Rosetta's cameras lost track of it. Scientists figured it was stuck in a shady spot where sunlight couldn't reach its solar panels. Because it was solar-powered, Philae needed to be facing the sun properly to generate enough power for sustained operation on the comet's surface.

Still, Philae did have some power stored in batteries, which lasted for more than two days on the surface. That allowed Philae to perform some science with its 10 instruments in the time it had on Comet 67/P. Most notably, Philae found organic molecules that had never been detected on a comet before.

The Rosetta orbiter continued to orbit Comet 67P until September 2016, and it was in that month -- just weeks before Rosetta itself landed on the comet on Sept. 30, 2016 -- that the spacecraft rediscovered the Philae lander lying on its side in a rocky crevice.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky? ]]> SpaceX's Starship megarocket is slated to launch on its ambitious 15th flight test as soon as this Friday (Nov. 13). Will you be able to spot its leviathan upper stage, known as Ship, or its Starlink satellite passengers as they circle Earth during the historic orbital jaunt?

Flight 15's 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT) on Nov. 13. Starship will fly from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, where it will be 4:45 p.m. at the opening of the window — about an hour before sunset. The launch could therefore be especially dramatic for folks in the area.

"As it launches towards the southeast, and it will be daylight, then the prospects for viewing from the U.S. are going to be in Texas and the states along the Gulf of Mexico," Robert Massey, deputy executive director at the Royal Astronomical Society, told Space.com. "They could see the exhaust plume (the 'jellyfish') with the sky darker for observers further east."

If all goes to plan, Starship's Super Heavy booster will propel the Ship upper stage through the densest part of Earth's atmosphere before returning to Starbase for a powered landing and capture via the "chopstick" arms of the "Mechazilla" tower system. Ship, meanwhile, will go on to orbit Earth approximately 14 times over the following 22 hours, during which time it will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before returning to Starbase for its own ambitious catch attempt.

When should I look for Starship and its Starlink train?

Satellite visibility in the night sky depends on a cocktail of factors, from the size of the spacecraft to its reflectivity, orbital inclination and position relative to the Earth and sun.

Ship is big — about 171 feet (52 meters) tall — so it will be a viable target for skywatchers, experts say.

"It certainly will be visible in twilight hours. It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size," professor James Osborn of Durham University told Space.com. "Where and when is a bit more tricky."

Ship and its Starlink satellites may be seen in the 90 minutes directly after sunset on Nov. 13 and before sunrise on Nov. 14, as the probes catch the sunlight on either side of Earth's colossal shadow as they drift through the twilight sky.

The spacecraft will initially appear as a string of bright, evenly spaced lights, with Ship most likely appearing significantly brighter than the Starlink satellites. However, Osborn noted that the lack of publicly available data makes it challenging to forecast exactly when the spacecraft will appear.

"During its 14 orbits over 22 hours, the spacecraft is between inclinations of 30.5 [degrees] N and S of the equator," explained Massey. "So it will be best viewed between those latitudes, and then lower in the sky up to latitudes of 40 N and 40 S. That's pretty much the whole of the contiguous U.S."

Space.com skywatching columnist and veteran meteorologist Joe Rao shared further details on what stargazers may see with the naked eye as Ship drifts silently through the autumn sky.

"When it passes overhead, it will look like a bright, fast-moving star crossing the sky — similar to the International Space Station, but potentially even brighter depending on its orientation," explained Rao. "The Starlink V3 satellites are much smaller, so not as bright, perhaps ranging anywhere from 2nd to 4th magnitude, depending on the angle of illumination with reflected light from the sun."

Magnitude is the scale used by astronomers to measure the brightness of objects in the night sky. The lower the magnitude, the brighter the object! The unaided eye can make out objects with a magnitude of around +6.5 under ideal dark sky conditions, while the planet Venus currently shines at magnitude -4.41.

The Starlink train will likely fall further behind Starship as the 22-hour mission progresses, while the train itself will become more elongated, according to Rao. "For locations where it will make a high arc across the sky, the Starship should be visible for at least a few minutes, although because it is orbiting at a lower altitude (170 miles/275 km) compared to the ISS, it probably will appear to move somewhat faster. "

How can I track Starship after launch?

There are multiple handy resources that should allow you to track Ship and the newly deployed batch of V3 Starlink satellites following their scheduled launch on Nov. 13, including the websites Heavens-Above, Star Dash, Orbital Radar and Find Starlink.

"It certainly will be visible in twilight hours. It should be very bright, considerably brighter than the Starlink satellites due to its size," professor James Osborn of Durham University told Space.com. "Where and when is a bit more tricky."

The spacecraft will initially appear as a string of bright, evenly spaced lights, with Ship most likely appearing significantly brighter than the Starlink satellites. However, Osborn noted that the lack of publicly available data makes it challenging to forecast exactly when the spacecraft will appear.

"During its 14 orbits over 22 hours, the spacecraft is between inclinations of 30.5 [degrees] N and S of the equator," explained Massey. Magnitude is the scale used by astronomers to measure the brightness of objects in the night sky. The lower the magnitude, the brighter the object! ]]> <![CDATA[ 'Warhammer Survivors' is the perfect gateway into the 40K universe ]]> We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium.

Developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this new spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes.

When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into.

Warhammer Survivors isn't bogged down by dense lore, involved mechanics, or massive campaign playthroughs. It's more of an "inspired by" effort that gives casuals a small taste of the series' iconic characters — including Boltgun's Malum Caedo — and factions like the terrifying Tyranids, the raucous Orks, and the foul forces of Chaos.

All of 40K's (and Age of Sigmar's) recognizable elements are on display, but they serve more as flavoring sprinkled on top of Vampire Survivors' successful formula.

If you're new to the Survivors-like subgenre, it's a unique gaming experience. You battle an endless onslaught of enemies that slowly march towards you, with your character passively attacking automatically. You only need to move them around sprawling arenas and select level-up upgrades and items after collecting enough gems (skulls in this case).

The moment-to-moment gameplay is as simple as it can get outside of walking sims and interactive "experiences," but there's a deceiving depth to item synergies and how to correctly "build" characters to endure all the carnage.

Unlike Poncle's original game, Warhammer Survivors struggles a bit to get going. The early hours are sluggish until you unlock certain meta upgrades, but its still got that Vampire Survivors magic at its core.

As far as "podcast/gym games" go, this is a perfect fit. There's just enough going on to keep one's brain engaged, but minimal inputs and a tight overarching design lead to a rhythm that's easy to get into without using much brainpower. It's oddly satisfying to weave through enemies and level up your firepower, watching a single Astra Militarum grunt grow into a full Lasgun-spamming, chainsword-wielding wrecking ball.

Achievement and unlock hunters will find enough to bite into here, too. It's unclear if the devs will continue to add more Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar deep cuts to this game via DLCs and free updates, but those universes have daunting depths to explore. This really could become a gateway game for future 40K fans: by the time they realize they're hooked, they'll already have 2000 pts of space marines painted and ready to play.

As massive sci-fi and fantasy properties try to aggressively expand and absorb more and more fans, it's easy to pander to already-converted diehards too much. And sure, we can't wait for strategy heavyweights like Dawn of War 4 and Total War: WH40K either, but they're hardly good recommendations for folks who don't even know what a Space Marine is or why the robotic Necrons are so grumpy.

Warhammer Survivors won't answer those questions beyond the surface-level iconography, but it's fun enough to push those curious to dig deeper and embrace the same material in more mature video game genres... and maybe even pick up a few miniatures.

Warhammer Survivors is now available on PC (Steam & GOG), PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 1/2, and mobile (iOS & Android). It's also playable on Game Pass.

]]> <![CDATA[ Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video) ]]>

On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter.

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter, the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy, the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe.

The new data release, designated DR1-Foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023.

"These are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," ESA's Director of Science, Carole Mundell said in a statement. "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration."

What's in the Euclid release

The ESA put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the Dark Universe Detective and contained in DR1-Foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars, regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes.

"This is a change in scale from Euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," ESA's Euclid project scientist Valeria Pettorino said. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. This unlocks groundbreaking science."

Euclid can see such a vast number of cosmic objects thanks to the fact that its space-based position helps it avoid interference caused by Earth's atmosphere.

This includes clusters of galaxies and even larger superclusters. The study of these objects, some of the largest structures in the cosmos, can reveal how matter came together across the larger network of gas, dust and dark matter called the cosmic web.

"Euclid doesn't just look far back in time  — it does so across huge areas of sky," Euclid Consortium member Barbara Sartoris of JL Lagrange Laboratory, Nice, France, explained. "This gives us an unprecedented view of large samples of ancient galaxy clusters that were previously out of reach.

"We will explore these in the coming months to learn how these giants grew, and decipher what they reveal about the dark universe."

Another exciting element of the new Euclid data release is the 15,000 strong gravitational lensing candidates catalogued by the space telescope. Gravitational lensing is an element of the universe first explained in Einstein magnum opus, general relativity, in 1915.

General relativity says that objects with mass cause the very fabric of space to warp, and that gravity arises from this warping. But there is another consequence. When light passes this curvature, its usually straight path is curved. That means when light from a single background source passes an object with great mass, like a galaxy or galaxy cluster, a strong gravitational lens, it can arrive at our telescopes at different times.

As a result of this strong lensing, background sources can be greatly amplified. It is an effect that the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has been using to great effect to study galaxies in the early universe.

Thus, the prospect of mapping 15,000 strong gravitational lenses is monumental, especially in studying the rate at which the universe is expanding and thus the effect of dark energy.

"Strong lensing provides unique insight into the dark universe, allowing us to 'weigh' individual galaxies, including their invisible dark matter, and explore how the universe is expanding," Natalie Lines of the University of Portsmouth, U.K., and member of the Euclid Consortium, said. "Over 10 years ago, we forecast that Euclid would revolutionize the field of strong lens discovery. That day is finally here."

The best is yet to come

Arguably, the most exciting thing about DR1-Foundation is that Euclid is just getting started. The area of sky covered from spring 2024 to spring 2025 represents just 14% of Euclid's target for its entire six-year survey.

That means whatever scientists discover from this data release could be the tip of the iceberg in terms of how the Dark Universe Detective will change our understanding of the cosmos.

"DR1-Foundation includes raw data, calibrated images, catalogues, and spectra over a huge sky area, with enough statistics touncover even rare objects," Valeria said. "It will be used to map the large-scale structure of the universe in unprecedented detail.

"So much discovery is yet to come."

]]> <![CDATA[ Pakistani astronaut set to become 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station this month ]]> An astronaut from Pakistan is set to launch on China's Shenzhou 24 mission in the coming weeks and become the first-ever international visitor to the Tiangong space station.

A pair of astronaut candidates from Pakistan have been training at the Astronaut Centre of China in Beijing, following an agreement reached between China and Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 and a subsequent selection process.

China's human spaceflight agency confirmed in a Nov. 7 press statement that the upcoming Shenzhou 24 mission will carry one of the astronauts. The agency also released a mission patch.

"China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Nov. 9. "Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China's spaceships will mark the first-ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program."

It is not yet known which of the two candidates will fly on Shenzhou 24. They were named in Pakistani press reports as Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, both pilots from the country's military forces. The pair were chosen from a wider pool of around 20 finalists.

The chosen candidate will fly as a payload specialist on Shenzhou 24 along with two Chinese colleagues, while the other will be on standby as a backup. While the Chinese astronauts will be starting a six-month-long stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will spend roughly a week in orbit aboard Tiangong during a standard crew rotation period. He will then return to Earth aboard the departing Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with two Chinese astronauts who will have completed a six-month-long stay in orbit.

The arrangement means changes to China's usual "three in, three out" Tiangong crew rotations. One of the three Shenzhou 23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong on May 24, will stay aboard and complete China's first-ever year-long stay in orbit, while the Pakistani astronaut will take their seat aboard Shenzhou 23 to return home.

During his stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will be responsible for four research payloads selected from more than 300 proposals, according to Pakistan's space agency, SUPARCO.

China has not announced a timeline for the launch of the Shenzhou 24 mission, but it is expected to lift off before the end of November. The Shenzhou 23 astronauts currently aboard Tiangong are closing in on 180 days in orbit, nearing an end to their six months in space.

Shenzhou 24 will launch from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in the Gobi Desert on a Long March 2F rocket. The identities of the crew for China's human spaceflight missions are typically closely guarded, and will only be revealed in a press conference a day ahead of launch. Shenzhou 24's Long March 2F rocket will be rolled out to the pad around a week ahead of launch.

The partnership between the two countries has already produced Chinese-launched Pakistani satellites, including a lunar cubesat, and a Pakistani-built rover due to fly on the Chang'e-8 lunar landing mission.

]]> <![CDATA[ The replicants are running the city in thrilling final trailer for ‘Blade Runner 2099’ (video) ]]>

One of the most anticipated fall TV series, "Blade Runner 2099," recently dropped its final neon-tinted trailer, and now we’ve finally got a handle on the plot dynamics of this dystopian thriller set in the cyberpunk world of Ridley Scott's original.

Prime Video's bold and brooding 8-episode series lands Nov. 25 as a tangential sequel to Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049," unfolding some 50 years after the 2017 feature film. Now the artificial inmates are running the asylum when violent replicant uprisings flip the script, causing humanity to become second-class citizens.

"In Los Angeles 2099, Cora (Hunter Schafer) lived her entire life on the run, a chameleon forced to adopt numerous identities," states Prime Video's synopsis. "To secure a stable future for her brother, she assumes one final identity and is forced to partner with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Blade Runner who’s confronting the end of her life. The two are pulled into a widening conspiracy that poses an existential threat to a city that’s fighting to be reborn."

This engrossing final trailer reveals more of the detailed noir world and Cora's plight to blend into society as a Blade Runner who links up with Olwen, an aging replicant exterminator, for an uneasy partnership. Here, a tense scene plays out in this preview as Cora undergoes an intense police station screening while being used as a resistance pawn to help take back the city from usurping androids. But another deep mystery lies hidden in plain sight!

"You have to see the lie that is in front of you," warns Yeoh's dying synthetic cop.

"Blade Runner 2099" sports a spirited cast that includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) in collaboration with Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”).

Delivered by creator and showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls"), and executive produced by Silka Louisa and Ridley Scott’s Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" lands on Prime Video beginning Nov. 25, 2026.

 <description>Soudy mohou už téměř rok nařídit nájemníkům bez platné smlouvy vystěhovat se z bytu díky novému nástroji. Takzvaný rozkaz k vyklizení měl celý proces zrychlit.  <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/nejlepsi-skolni-jidelna-u-nas-kritizuje-zruseni-vyhlasky-pro-nas-se-nic-nemeni_2611130800_eml</link>
 <description>Víc zeleniny, ovoce a ryb. A naopak míň polotovarů nebo sladkých nápojů. Tak měly od příštího září vypadat obědy ve školních jídelnách. Jenže vláda nečekaně otočila – nová pravidla nakonec povinná nebudou. Takzvaný spotřební koš, který určuje složení jídelníčku, se má stát jen doporučením. Zrušení vyhlášky nechápe vedení školní jídelny v Boršicích na Uherskohradišťsku, která se pyšní letošním titulem nejlepší školní jídelny v Česku.</description>

   <description>Čekání ve frontách na dopravních úřadech by mohlo být brzy minulostí. Ministerstvo dopravy chystá legislativní změnu, díky které vyřídíte přepis auta nebo novou registraci kompletně z domova.  <description>Ukrajinské protikorupční agentury NABU a SAP v září spustily operaci, kterou nazvaly Kartágo. Vyšetřovatelé se v ní zaměřují na činnost podvodných call center. Minulý týden přišli se zjištěním, že do jejich krytí před ukrajinskými úřady byli zapojení i nejvyšší představitelé bezpečnostních složek, včetně tajné služby nebo prokuratury.  <description>Severokorejští hackeři podporovaní státem ukradli za posledních 18 měsíců kryptoměny v hodnotě více než 400 milionů dolarů (8,7 miliardy korun), přičemž zneužili tajně pořízené záznamy z webkamer. Při podvodech hackeři údajně využívali i nástroje umělé inteligence, které jim pomáhaly vydávat se za jiné osoby při videohovorech. Severní Korea se k obvinění zatím nevyjádřila.</description>

Stavba necelé dva kilometry dlouhého úseku přinesla dlouhou uzavírku a vyšla na více než půl miliardy korun.</description></item><item><title>Víkend přinese slunce. Poté se vrátí déšť</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905654-vikend-prinese-slunce-pote-se-vrati-dest.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905654-vikend-prinese-slunce-pote-se-vrati-dest.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nadcházející víkend slibuje sice nižší teploty, ale návrat slunečného počasí. Začátkem příštího týdne se pak dokonce oteplí, ale s oteplením přijde návrat dešťových srážek.</description></item><item><title>Neviděli jste tuto ženu? Ztratila se v Liberci, pátrá po ní policie i rodina</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905659-nevideli-jste-tuto-zenu-ztratila-se-v-liberci-patra-po-ni-policie-i-rodina.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905659-nevideli-jste-tuto-zenu-ztratila-se-v-liberci-patra-po-ni-policie-i-rodina.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:49:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Po 73leté Václavě Forstové z Liberce pátrá od čtvrtečního večera rodina, policie a během noci se přidaly i desítky dobrovolníků. Žena byla naposledy viděna v okolí svého bydliště v blízkosti muzea, na sobě má zelenou nebo žlutou bundu. Pokud ji zahlédnete, ihned kontaktujte policii na lince 158.</description></item><item><title>Zubní pohotovosti v Liberci zůstávají. Jedna je v Dunaji, druhá v nemocnici</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905595-zubni-pohotovosti-v-liberci-zustavaji-jedna-je-v-dunaji-druha-v-nemocnici.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905595-zubni-pohotovosti-v-liberci-zustavaji-jedna-je-v-dunaji-druha-v-nemocnici.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 06:25:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Dobrá zpráva pro pacienty v Libereckém kraji. Obě zubní pohotovosti v Liberci, ta v paláci Dunaj i ta v areálu Krajské nemocnice Liberec, v příštím roce zůstávají. K dispozici jsou těm, kteří potřebují řešit akutní bolest zubů o víkendech a svátcích, každá v jinou dobu. Jedna na druhou navazuje.</description></item><item><title>Také vám volají s nabídkami, o které nestojíte? Víme, jak otravné hovory utnout</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905613-take-vam-volaji-s-nabidkami-o-ktere-nestojite-vime-jak-otravne-hovory-utnout.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905613-take-vam-volaji-s-nabidkami-o-ktere-nestojite-vime-jak-otravne-hovory-utnout.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 19:09:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Zazvoní telefon a na druhém konci se ozve nabídka výhodnějšího tarifu, levnější energie nebo finančních služeb. Přestože jste o žádnou nabídku nežádali, volající zná vaše jméno či další osobní údaje. Kde obchodníci získávají telefonní čísla, kdy vás mohou kontaktovat a co dělat, aby už nevolali?</description></item><item><title>Geografický střed Jizerek nově připomíná skoro tunový žulový kámen</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905566-geograficky-stred-jizerek-nove-pripomina-skoro-tunovy-zulovy-kamen.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905566-geograficky-stred-jizerek-nove-pripomina-skoro-tunovy-zulovy-kamen.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Jizerské hory mají nově označený přesný geografický střed. Ten se nachází nedaleko Soušské silnice přibližně mezi Smědavou a přehradou Souš a na jeho místě nadšenci instalovali 900 kilogramů těžký žulový kámen.</description></item><item><title>Modernizace si vyžaduje technické pracovníky. V Ontexu hledají nové kolegy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905509-modernizace-si-vyzaduje-technicke-pracovniky-v-ontexu-hledaji-nove-kolegy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905509-modernizace-si-vyzaduje-technicke-pracovniky-v-ontexu-hledaji-nove-kolegy.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Výrobce hygienického zboží Ontex hledá do svého provozu v Turnově nové kolegy. Firma má přitom co nabídnout, ať už jde o dlouhou historii, moderní stroje nebo širokou paletu benefitů.</description></item><item><title>Liberecká ZŠ Husova nové výživové standardy zkoušela v září, děti obědy nejedly</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/905583-liberecka-zs-husova-nove-vyzivove-standardy-zkousela-v-zari-deti-obedy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/905583-liberecka-zs-husova-nove-vyzivove-standardy-zkousela-v-zari-deti-obedy.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Děti obědy nechtěly a vracely, takovou zkušenost získali kuchaři Základní školy Husova v Liberci s novými výživovými standardy pro školní stravování, když podle nich zkoušeli v září vařit. Ředitelka školy Blanka Reindlová proto vítá, že standardy budou nadále nezávazným doporučením.</description></item><item><title>Deset let za volantem. Kurýrka Gabriela zná svoji trasu jako málokdo</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904895-deset-let-za-volantem-kuryrka-gabriela-zna-svoji-trasu-jako-malokdo.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904895-deset-let-za-volantem-kuryrka-gabriela-zna-svoji-trasu-jako-malokdo.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:54:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Modrou škodovkou už projezdila Prahu křížem krážem. Kurýrka Woltu Gabriela Dvořáková vozí jídlo seniorům, pacientům v nemocnicích i známým hercům. Práce jí vyhovuje hlavně proto, že si sama určuje, kdy jezdí.</description></item><item><title>Poslanecký přílepek ohrožuje vodovody a kanalizace v malých obcích. Kraj se bouří</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905575-poslanecky-prilepek-ohrozuje-vodovody-a-kanalizace-v-malych-obcich-kraj-se-bouri.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905575-poslanecky-prilepek-ohrozuje-vodovody-a-kanalizace-v-malych-obcich-kraj-se-bouri.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:56:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberecký kraj zásadně odmítá poslanecký návrh, který by regionům bez náhrady odebral podíl z poplatků za odběr podzemní vody. Podle vedení kraje by to ochromilo výstavbu vodovodů a kanalizací v malých obcích, kde už nyní třetina sídel čistírnu či kanalizaci postrádá.</description></item></channel></rss>

Ve středu 11. listopadu 2026 se ve varnsdorfské tělocvičně uskutečnilo 4. kolo Podzimních her, tentokrát v košíkové. Do turnaje se zapojila družstva dívek a chlapců ze čtyř škol, která mezi sebou změřila síly a předvedla řadu napínavých sportovních soubojů.

Turnaj se hrál systémem každý s každým, přičemž jednotlivá utkání trvala 2 × 8 minut. Na palubovce nechybělo nasazení, bojovnost, týmová spolupráce ani touha po vítězství.

Dvě stříbrná umístění pro naši školu!

Naši žáci a žákyně ze ZŠ Náměstí předvedli krásné, bojovné a obětavé výkony. V každém utkání nechali na hřišti maximum, bojovali o každý míč a ukázali, že týmový duch a vzájemná podpora jsou základem úspěchu.

Velkou radost nám udělala obě naše družstva, která si v silné konkurenci vybojovala shodně krásné 2. místo! Všem našim hráčům a hráčkám patří velká pochvala a poděkování za parádní reprezentaci školy. Jsme na vás pyšní!

Děkujeme také všem zúčastněným školám za pěkné sportovní souboje a těšíme se na další kolo Podzimních her!
